title: Detect hand-written records: fabricated jobs, forged landings, proposals
summary: Add a gate-enforced provenance mechanism (assumed: a keyed MAC or witness ledger held in the user's state dir, outside the repo) so the three forgeries named in design §16.2 and acceptance-2 (fully hand-made job, forged landing of a dispatched-but-unclosed job, hand-made proposal closed with `athena close`) are detected, with tests replaying each and docs updated.

defaults_applied.how: Tests for each of the three forgery routes plus a genuine-job regression; cargo test, clippy, fmt clean.
Criterion requires a written design with alternatives for the mechanism.
Criteria replay the forgeries and check they are caught, not that types exist.
Any MAC/hash crate must be an adopted one, with the call recorded.
Detection is enforced in the gate, not prose.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Goal: close the three residuals in design §16.2 so that hand-written records no longer pass the gate; audience is the user/maintainer and the independent verifier who will replay the forgeries from acceptance-2.

Detection means a mechanism that distinguishes Athena-written records from hand-written ones using a secret or ledger Athena holds outside the repository (user state dir), not full tamper-proofing; a deliberate forger who reads that state can still defeat it, and docs say so.
Where the key/ledger is absent (CI, fresh clone), the gate behaves as today for already-landed history, with a bootstrap boundary like the existing exempt range, so old history is not broken.
Exact mechanism is left to the producer's design; the reading does not prescribe MAC versus ledger.

acceptance_criteria.text: A design note (new file under docs/design/, or a section in athena-v0.md) states the chosen detection mechanism, at least two alternatives considered (e.g. keyed MAC over records with a key in the user's state dir; local append-only witness ledger of record hashes; signing), and why one was chosen. It states what it still cannot stop: a forger who reads the key or ledger.

A test constructs a job written entirely by hand, record by record across two commits with reconciling usage, and shows `athena check --history` (and the commit-msg hook path) now reports it. Run `cargo test` and see that it passes.
A test forges a landing for a job that was read and dispatched but never closed (single commit adding the hand change and four closing records) and shows the gate refuses it. Run `cargo test`.
A test shows a hand-made proposal commit closed with `athena close` is refused or flagged and does not move its class's calibration headline. Run `cargo test`.

A genuine job produced with the fake agent still lands, closes, scores and passes `athena check --history` unchanged; existing gate and CLI tests still pass. Run `cargo test`, `cargo clippy` and `cargo fmt --check`, all clean.

Design §16.2 and docs/enforcement.md are updated: the three listed forgery routes are marked detectable, and any remaining residual (deliberate theft of the key or ledger) is stated plainly. CHANGELOG.md records the change.
Any new crate dependency (e.g. for HMAC) is a maintained crate, and the buy-first call is recorded; no secret or key material is committed.

out_of_scope: Full cryptographic signing with external identity (e.g. GPG/sigstore) or branch protection
Containment of executed code (the other §16.2 residuals)
Requiring totals on outcomes beyond what the forgery fixes need
Re-writing or invalidating existing landed history
departures: Touches gate, core store and close paths plus design docs; larger and riskier than the typical job, and the mechanism choice is open, so cost, time and pass probability are worse than reference.
